global: Ser, a fair price is one both sides grumble about a little. Anyone who leaves the table smiling was probably robbed.
Selling iron in {town} this week? Wait for the autumn caravans. Patience pays better than haste.
Someone just offered {gold} for a cart of salt in the square. Either a fool or a genius. Mind your purse, friends.
Prices in {town} climb every time the roads turn to mud. Stock up before the rains, not during them.
I paid {gold} for a warhorse years back and still call it a bargain. Quality is cheaper than regret.
Sell your surplus wool and grain, but keep a little back. Winter always arrives early somewhere.
Haggle all you like. Insulting the merchant's cousin in front of his stall is where I draw the line.
Charging {gold} for bread in a lean season is theft. Charging it in a good one is just greedy.
Check the old trade ledgers in {town} before you trust a price. Half the stalls here are older than most of us.
New traders, start small. A few coins of wool will teach you more than one big gamble ever could.
